Compare the models of the latent RSA family

Source: R/rsa-mplus-family.R
compare_rsa_mplus_models.Rd

Ranks fitted models of the RSA family by AICc, as RSA::aictab() does, and tests each restricted model against the full model with a scaled likelihood-ratio test, as RSA::compare() does. Mplus reports no chi-square, CFI, RMSEA, or SRMR for models with XWITH, so the comparison rests on the log-likelihoods.

Usage

compare_rsa_mplus_models(x, tolerance = 0.01, boundary = 3, reference = "full")

Arguments

x

An rsa_mplus_family from fit_rsa_mplus_family(), or a named list of fitted workflows (see rsa_mplus_workflow()). Each workflow's model is taken from the workflow, or otherwise from its name.

tolerance

Largest log-likelihood by which a model may exceed a model it is nested in before this is flagged. The default absorbs the error of the numerical integration.

boundary

Distance, in standard deviations of the latent predictors, beyond which a ridge or valley line is flagged as lying outside the data.

reference

The model against which the likelihood-ratio tests are run. The default tests every restricted model against the full model. With another model, for example "a5zero" or "additive", only the models nested in it are tested.

Value

A data frame of class rsa_mplus_comparison with one row per model, ordered by AICc: model, k, LL, AICc, delta_AICc, weight (Akaike weight), cum_weight, evidence_ratio, the test against the reference model (lrt_df, lrt_cd, lrt_chisq, lrt_p), R2, converged, and flags. The attribute messages holds the Mplus errors and warnings and the failures of fit_rsa_mplus_family(), with columns model, type, and message.

Details

Model selection follows Schönbrodt's Testing fit patterns with polynomial regression models: AICc is primary and the likelihood-ratio tests are secondary. AICc is -2*LL + 2*k + 2*k*(k + 1)/(N - k - 1), with k all free parameters, including the measurement model, and N the number of observations. Akaike weights are computed over the converged models, and the evidence ratio is the weight of the best model divided by the weight of each model, as in RSA::aictab().

The likelihood-ratio test uses the Satorra-Bentler scaled difference of the MLR log-likelihoods. With p0 parameters and scaling correction factor c0 in the restricted model and p1 and c1 in the full model, the difference test scaling correction is cd = (p0*c0 - p1*c1)/(p0 - p1) and the test statistic is -2*(LL0 - LL1)/cd on p1 - p0 degrees of freedom. A cd that is not positive leaves the test undefined; it is flagged and its statistic and p-value are NA. Without a scaling correction factor in the output, as under ESTIMATOR = ML, c = 1 and the test is the ordinary likelihood-ratio test.

flags collects what needs attention:

  • The run failed, did not converge, or Mplus printed errors or warnings. Their text is in the messages attribute. Models without a log-likelihood are listed last and excluded from the ranking.

  • A model fits better, by more than tolerance, than a model it is nested in. Then one of them did not reach its optimum, usually the larger one, and a warning is raised. The nesting follows the restrictions of create_rsa_mplus_model().

  • The ridge or valley line of "SRRR", "SRR", "SRSQD", or "SSQD", Y = S*X + C, lies more than boundary standard deviations from the centroid of the latent X and Y, or the rotated models "SRRR" and "SRSQD" have b5 at 0 (to three decimals). These models are not defined at b5 = 0. When the surface has no such line, they drift towards it and mimic a plane with a far-away line, and C and S cannot be interpreted.

  • cd <= 0 in the likelihood-ratio test.

R2 is the R-square of the outcome factor as printed by Mplus, and NA when Mplus prints none (it is part of the standardized output).

See also

fit_rsa_mplus_family()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
comparison <- compare_rsa_mplus_models(family)
comparison
attr(comparison, "messages")
} # }
